description_paragraphs: The base error is $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2$. The tolerance $\varepsilon$ is always expressed on the gradient-norm scale. The mean-square requirement is equivalent to the RMS gradient being at most this tolerance.

In this unconstrained model with a strongly convex lower level, $
abla\Phi(x)=
abla_x f(x,y^*)-g_{xy}(x,y^*)g_{yy}(x,y^*)^{-1}
abla_y f(x,y^*)$, where $g_{xy}=\mathrm{D}_y
abla_x g$ and $g_{yy}=\mathrm{D}_y
abla_y g$, and $y^*$ denotes $y^*(x)$. The identity defines the hypergradient without granting additional query access.
metric.finiteness_conditions: Guaranteed by the model and the associated differentiability result, not inferred from an oracle-order label alone.
metric.normalization: The tolerance is on the gradient-norm scale. This contract requires $\mathbb E\|\nabla\Phi\|^2\le\epsilon^2$.

assumptions.description: The upper objective is $f=n_f^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_f}f_i$. Its components may be nonconvex.
Assume $g=(1/n_g)\sum_{j=1}^{n_g}g_j$; per-component strong convexity ensures uniqueness of the lower-level mean solution.
Each $f_i$ is twice differentiable. Function values, full gradients, and full Hessians have the respective global joint Lipschitz budgets $L^F_0,L^F_1,L^F_2$, uniformly across components.

Every $g_j$ is three times differentiable. The full first, second, and third derivatives have the respective global joint Lipschitz budgets $L^G_1,L^G_2,L^G_3$. Every $g_j(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu$-strongly convex, uniformly over components.

The objective $\Phi$ is bounded below. The source initial Lyapunov quantity minus $\inf\Phi$ has public finite upper bound $V_0$, fixed independently of accuracy and component counts. It includes the upper-level gap, lower-level value gap, and an adjoint quadratic potential.

The initial SRBA adjoint vector $v_0$ lies in the known ball $\|v_0\|\le L^F_0/\mu$. Subsequent projections apply only to this auxiliary vector; x and y may still be queried throughout their Euclidean spaces. Projection onto this known ball is an arithmetic operation, not a hidden projection oracle.

model.initial_potential_definition: Let $H(x)=g_{yy}(x,y^*(x))$, $v^*(x)=-H(x)^{-1}f_y(x,y^*(x))$, and $\Psi_x(v)=\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}H(x)v+f_y(x,y^*(x))^{\mathsf T}v$. The source potential is $\Phi(x)+\psi_z[g(x,y)-\min_zg(x,z)]+\psi_v[\Psi_x(v)-\Psi_x(v^*(x))]$, where $\psi_z,\psi_v$ are fixed positive proof weights. The initial adjoint lies in the ball of radius $L^F_0/\mu$.

description_paragraphs: Public inputs are dimension, target accuracy, the model's budgets, and the initial point. The original functions, their lower-level solutions, and the reduced objective are hidden. Queries are restricted to the stated interfaces; inner optima and undeclared derivatives are not available for free.

The interface returns $(i,x,y), i\in\{1,\ldots,n_f\}\longmapsto \nabla f_i(x,y)$: exact derivatives or derivative–vector products of a selected component. No fresh population-noise oracle is supplied.
$(j,x,y), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}\longmapsto \nabla g_j(x,y)$. Return the exact derivative or derivative-vector action of the selected component. No fresh noisy population oracle is provided.

$(j,x,y,v), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}, v\in R^{d_y}\longmapsto (g_j)_{xy}(x,y)v$. Return the exact derivative or derivative-vector product of the selected component. There is no fresh noisy population oracle.
$(j,x,y,v), j\in\{1,\ldots,n_g\}, v\in R^{d_y}\longmapsto (g_j)_{yy}(x,y)v$ The selected component's derivative or derivative-vector action is exact. No fresh noisy population oracle is provided.
The same component index may be used at consecutive iterates. Every operation is still charged separately.

description_paragraphs: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

proofs.proof: Retain the frozen joint Euclidean norm conventions and native hypergradient identity. A differentiable L^F_0-Lipschitz component has gradient norm at most L^F_0; averaging preserves this bound for f. Differentiating each L^G_1-Lipschitz gradient gives ||Hess g_j||<=L^G_1, hence ||Hess g||<=L^G_1 after averaging. At (x,y*(x)), write Hess g=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], with C>=mu I. Set k=L^G_1/mu>=1 for a nonempty admissible class. For every w, applying Hess g to (0,C^-1 w) gives ||D C^-1 w||^2+||w||^2 <= (L^G_1)^2 ||C^-1 w||^2 <= k^2 ||w||^2. Thus ||D C^-1||<=sqrt(k^2-1), and the row operator [I,-D C^-1] has norm at most k. The native identity grad Phi=f_x-D C^-1 f_y now yields ||grad Phi(x)||<=L^F_0 k at every x. Output the public outer initial point x0 without querying any interface. The contract requires neither an inner point nor a computed certificate; no initialization oracle responses are needed to return x0. For epsilon>=L^F_0 k the deterministic squared-gradient error is <=epsilon^2, including equality. All four response counts are zero on every execution. Nonnegative response costs imply Q*>=0, so Q*=0 on this sufficient region. The proof covers L^F_0=0. It asserts no converse below the threshold and is uniform in sample counts and dimensions; it uses no V_0 premise.

Aggregate summary counts are the histogram of these actual native states; missing sides are their union; only logarithmic_gap, polynomial_gap and other_quantified_gap belong to gap_classes. summary: Solve the bilevel problem $\min_x\Phi(x)$, where $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^*(x))$ and $y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y g(x,y)$ is the unique global lower-level solution. The upper- and lower-level variables are $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. Seek approximate stationarity of the reduced objective under the declared criterion and guarantee; assumptions on $f$, $g$, and $\Phi$ are specified separately.

algorithms.adaptivity: arbitrary measurable functions of past responses
description_paragraphs: Algorithms may use private randomness. Queries, stopping, and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript. The output may be unqueried, a random selection of a past point, or an admissible average. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Queries are sequential; each actual response in a parallel batch is charged separately. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage using received data are uncharged. Internal operations, memory, and communication are not tracked by this quantity.
algorithms.internal_computation: This model counts only oracle resources. Arithmetic, linear algebra, and storage applied to received responses are free. Any extra hidden-function gradient, HVP/JVP, value, or inner-solve response must be obtained through a declared, charged operation.
algorithms.parallelism: sequential adaptive calls; simultaneous batch calls count separately

budget.budget_semantics: fixed worst-case total number of calls on every execution
budget.precision_model: Exact real arithmetic is assumed; the stochastic oracle has the stated noise. Bit complexity, memory, and arithmetic cost are not tracked.
budget.scalarization: $Q=N_{\nabla f}+N_{\nabla g}+N_{\rm JVP}+N_{\rm HVP}$, retaining all four resource coordinates. The source joint query and this total are equivalent only up to fixed constants. Full scans and repeated-component differences are charged.

aggregation_order: For each fixed admissible instance, first take expectation over oracle noise and private algorithmic randomness. The resulting guarantee must hold for every admissible instance.
description_paragraphs: Choose one algorithm from the public parameters, then require $\mathbb{E}\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2^2\le\varepsilon^2$ for every admissible instance and legal oracle law. Expectation includes all algorithmic and feedback randomness, with the instance fixed first.
guarantees.quantifier_order: A single algorithm family, depending only on public budgets and the interaction history, must meet the target for every admissible function and oracle law. Minimax quantifiers are infimum over algorithms followed by supremum over instances; the algorithm is not selected separately for each hidden instance.
randomness_sources: Private algorithmic randomness, including random selection of the output iterate
